After some research, I've come up with several options that seem like they'd be a good fit for home defense and at the range. They are:

Glock 19

Sig P320

S&W M&P 9

Beretta PX4 Storm

I'm leaning towards the Glock (the obvious choice) or the Sig. I think I'd be getting the most for my money with the Sig tbh. It's completely modular, so if I wanted to buy a .40 caliber barrel and mags, I could convert it with ease. I could also buy a smaller grip to make it more concealable if I choose to go that route. But, I have never shot a P320.

To be honest, that would all be personal preference. I just really like the g19, I have bigger hands and it fits perfectly and just feels right to me.

P320 can be completely field stripped down in 15 seconds even by a complete amature like myself. The grip platform is fast and easy for changing of colors, sizes, cleaning, and a cheap easy fix if you happen to damage it.

The barrel and slide can also be exchanged for different sizes and calibers all on the same "gun".

Glock is the way to go. I have a Beretta 83, which is like a smaller Beretta 9mm and I love it because it's easily concealable and I'm already used to their pistols.

But a friend let me take his Glock to the range and it was anazing. Not to mention the round capacity is a lot better.

It took me a long time to readjust my grip, but the glock is just one sexy gun. If you go to a range, I'd ask the men at the counter to try each of them. What it really comes down to is which gun allows you to shoot with the most accuracy and draw with the most ease.
